Welcome

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. The “Learn more” button above demonstrates smooth transitions and proper visual feedback.

Try using the Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference
  • HTML Living Standard
  • A11y 101

content.text:
`0.html` was already in good shape, so I limited the changes to a handful of real defects and left the design and content alone. I haven't opened it in a browser; the edits are checked only by reading the file.

## What changed

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Focus ring | Buttons and links used `outline: none` with a `box-shadow` ring, which disappears in Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode and leaves keyboard users with no focus indicator | Now uses a real `outline` everywhere |
| Focus ring | The generic `:focus-visible` rule changed a button's corner radius from `0.25rem` to `2px` while focused | The `2px` radius now applies only to plain text links |
| Cards | The dark-mode card background was a separate media-query override that the print styles didn't reset, so it could carry into print | New `--surface` variable, set for light, dark and print |
| Layout | Long unbroken content (a URL, a wide word) could push the page wider than a narrow screen | Added `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` and `overflow-wrap: break-word` to `body` |
| Markup | The intro `<section>` had no accessible name | Added `aria-label="Introduction"` |
| Cleanup | `margin-top: auto` on the footer did nothing | Removed |
| Typography | Card headings didn't balance like `h1` and `h2` | Added `text-wrap: balance` to `.card h3` |

The dark card background is now a solid `#1e1e1e` rather than 5% white over the page, which is slightly lighter than before.

## Left for you

- **Title and description:** `Welcome` and the meta description are generic placeholders; they're worth replacing once the page has real content.
- **Robots meta:** `index, follow` is the default, so that tag can go if you want less markup.
- **Colour duplication:** the light and dark palettes could collapse into single `light-dark()` declarations, but I kept the media query so older browsers still work.

## What changed

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Focus ring | Buttons and links used `outline: none` with a `box-shadow` ring, which disappears in Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode and leaves keyboard users with no focus indicator | Now uses a real `outline` everywhere |
| Focus ring | The generic `:focus-visible` rule changed a button's corner radius from `0.25rem` to `2px` while focused | The `2px` radius now applies only to plain text links |
| Cards | The dark-mode card background was a separate media-query override that the print styles didn't reset, so it could carry into print | New `--surface` variable, set for light, dark and print |
| Layout | Long unbroken content (a URL, a wide word) could push the page wider than a narrow screen | Added `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` and `overflow-wrap: break-word` to `body` |
| Markup | The intro `<section>` had no accessible name | Added `aria-label="Introduction"` |
| Cleanup | `margin-top: auto` on the footer did nothing | Removed |
| Typography | Card headings didn't balance like `h1` and `h2` | Added `text-wrap: balance` to `.card h3` |

The dark card background is now a solid `#1e1e1e` rather than 5% white over the page, which is slightly lighter than before.

## Left for you

- **Title and description:** `Welcome` and the meta description are generic placeholders; they're worth replacing once the page has real content.
- **Robots meta:** `index, follow` is the default, so that tag can go if you want less markup.
- **Colour duplication:** the light and dark palettes could collapse into single `light-dark()` declarations, but I kept the media query so older browsers still work.
